claim: Tumor initiation, progression and resistance to chemotherapy rely on cancer cells bypassing programmed cell death by apoptosis.
source: Tumor initiation, progression and resistance to chemotherapy rely on cancer cells bypassing programmed cell death by apoptosis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about cancer biology and apoptosis.

claim: Bim contains two distinct binding sites for the anti-apoptotic proteins Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
source: We report that unlike other pro-apoptotic proteins, Bim contains two distinct binding sites for the anti-apoptotic proteins Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: One Bim binding site is the BH3 sequence shared with other pro-apoptotic proteins.
source: These include the BH3 sequence shared with other pro-apoptotic proteins and an unexpected sequence located near the Bim carboxyl-terminus (residues 181–192).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and established knowledge about BH3 proteins.

claim: One Bim binding site is an unexpected sequence located near the Bim carboxyl-terminus (residues 181–192).
source: These include the BH3 sequence shared with other pro-apoptotic proteins and an unexpected sequence located near the Bim carboxyl-terminus (residues 181–192).
evidence: This is a novel finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The two binding interfaces enable Bim to double-bolt lock Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 in complexes resistant to displacement by BH3-mimetic drugs.
source: Using automated Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy - Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FLIM-FRET) we show that the two binding interfaces enable Bim to double-bolt lock Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 in complexes resistant to displacement by BH3-mimetic drugs currently in use or being evaluated for cancer therapy.
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Residue L185 previously thought involved in binding Bim to membranes instead contributes to binding to anti-apoptotic proteins.
source: Quantifying in live cells the contributions of individual amino acids revealed that residue L185 previously thought involved in binding Bim to membranes, instead contributes to binding to anti-apoptotic proteins.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from live cell measurements and in vitro assays.

claim: Bcl-2 family proteins regulate intrinsic apoptosis and mitochondrial integrity through direct physical interactions between anti-apoptotic proteins, pro-apoptotic proteins, and BH3-proteins.
source: Bcl-2 family proteins regulate intrinsic apoptosis and mitochondrial integrity through direct physical interactions between the anti-apoptotic proteins (Bcl-2, Bcl-XL and Mcl-1), the pro-apoptotic proteins (Bax, Bak) and the BH3-proteins (Bad, Bid and Bim) (Liu et al., 2013; Shamas-Din et al., 2013; Youle and Strasser, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In cancer cells, pro-apoptotic BH3 proteins and activated Bax and Bak are sequestered by anti-apoptotic proteins.
source: In cancer cells, pro-apoptotic BH3 proteins and activated Bax and Bak are sequestered by anti-apoptotic proteins, thereby the cell is protected at the same time as it is primed for death.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cancer cell biology.

claim: BH3-mimetic drugs can efficiently kill cancer cells by releasing bound pro-apoptotic proteins.
source: Such cells can be efficiently killed by BH3-mimetic drugs that release bound pro-apoptotic proteins, as shown by the clinical success of the Bcl-2 specific BH3-mimetics venetoclax (ABT-199) and navitoclax (ABT-263).
evidence: This is supported by clinical evidence and established knowledge.

claim: BH3 proteins bind to anti-apoptotic proteins exclusively through a conserved BH3 region.
source: It is commonly accepted that BH3 proteins bind to anti-apoptotic proteins exclusively through a conserved BH3 region (Chen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus supported by citation.

claim: ABT-263 is an orally available inhibitor with nanomolar affinity for the BH3-binding sites in Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
source: ABT-263 is an orally available inhibitor with nanomolar affinity for the BH3-binding sites in Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 that is currently undergoing clinical trials in humans.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the drug ABT-263.

claim: In vitro ABT-263 displaces BH3 peptides derived from different BH3-proteins including Bim from Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL.
source: In vitro ABT-263 displaces BH3 peptides derived from different BH3-proteins including Bim (Tse et al., 2008) from Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Increased expression of Bcl-XL in human non-Hodgkin lymphomas led to resistance to ABT-737 despite enhanced Bim expression.
source: 1) Increased expression of Bcl-XL in human non-Hodgkin lymphomas led to resistance to ABT-737 (an analogue of ABT-263) despite enhanced Bim expression (Mérino et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: FLIM-FRET demonstrated that ABT-263 displaced full-length Bad and tBid but not the major isoforms of Bim from binding to Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
source: 2) Fluorescent Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) – Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) demonstrated that ABT-263 displaced full-length Bad and tBid (activated Bid protein) but not the major isoforms of Bim (BimEL, BimL and BimS) from binding to Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 (Aranovich et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ABT-263 resistant binding of Bim to Bcl-XL was observed using bioluminescence resonance energy transfer.
source: 3) ABT-263 resistant binding of Bim to Bcl-XL was observed using bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (Pécot et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Bim is the only BH3-protein that binds all anti-apoptotic proteins with high affinities.
source: Among the Bcl-2 family, Bim is the only BH3-protein that binds all anti-apoptotic proteins with high affinities and that can directly activate Bax and Bak to initiate apoptosis (Chen et al., 2005; Letai et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Bim can directly activate Bax and Bak to initiate apoptosis.
source: Among the Bcl-2 family, Bim is the only BH3-protein that binds all anti-apoptotic proteins with high affinities and that can directly activate Bax and Bak to initiate apoptosis (Chen et al., 2005; Letai et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The lack of activity for BH3 mimetics on displacement of Bim could significantly reduce their efficacy in some cancer cells.
source: Therefore the surprising lack of activity for BH3 mimetics on displacement of Bim could significantly reduce their efficacy in some cancer cells (Pécot et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations and supported by citation.

claim: ABT-263 displaces VBad from CBcl-XL in MCF-7 cells.
source: ABT-263 displaced both VBad and VtBid, but not VBimEL from CBcl-XL (Figure 1D–F, compare green and cyan).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: ABT-263 displaces VtBid from CBcl-XL in MCF-7 cells.
source: ABT-263 displaced both VBad and VtBid, but not VBimEL from CBcl-XL (Figure 1D–F, compare green and cyan).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: ABT-263 does not displace VBimEL from CBcl-XL in MCF-7 cells.
source: ABT-263 displaced both VBad and VtBid, but not VBimEL from CBcl-XL (Figure 1D–F, compare green and cyan).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: BH3-2A mutations in VBad reduced binding to CBcl-XL dramatically.
source: As expected, BH3-2A mutations in VBad and VtBid reduced binding to CBcl-XL dramatically (Figure 1D–E, compare black and red).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: BH3-2A mutations in VtBid reduced binding to CBcl-XL dramatically.
source: As expected, BH3-2A mutations in VBad and VtBid reduced binding to CBcl-XL dramatically (Figure 1D–E, compare black and red).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The BH3-2A mutant of VBimEL bound to CBcl-XL similarly to wild-type VBimEL.
source: However the BH3-2A mutant of VBimEL bound to CBcl-XL similarly to wild-type VBimEL (Figure 1F, compare black and red), suggesting interactions with other residues contribute to binding Bim to Bcl-XL.
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: More than 80% of CBcl-XL:VBimEL complexes were resistant to the addition of ABT-263.
source: Plotting RABT-263 for different interactions indicated that >80% of CBcl-XL:VBimEL and CBcl-2:VBimEL complexes were resistant to the addition of ABT-263 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: More than 80% of CBcl-2:VBimEL complexes were resistant to the addition of ABT-263.
source: Plotting RABT-263 for different interactions indicated that >80% of CBcl-XL:VBimEL and CBcl-2:VBimEL complexes were resistant to the addition of ABT-263 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CBcl-XL:VBad complexes were less than 50% resistant to ABT-263.
source: In contrast, CBcl-XL:VBad and CBcl-XL:VtBid complexes were less than 50% resistant to the drug (Figure 2B-left, black)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CBcl-XL:VtBid complexes were less than 50% resistant to ABT-263.
source: In contrast, CBcl-XL:VBad and CBcl-XL:VtBid complexes were less than 50% resistant to the drug (Figure 2B-left, black)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Bcl-2:VBad complexes were less than 40% resistant to ABT-263.
source: while the corresponding Bcl-2 complexes were less than 40% resistant (Figure 2B-left, blue, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bcl-2:VtBid complexes were less than 40% resistant to ABT-263.
source: while the corresponding Bcl-2 complexes were less than 40% resistant (Figure 2B-left, blue, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A-1155463 and A-1331852 more potently disrupted CBcl-XL:VBad complexes compared to ABT-263.
source: Compared to ABT-263 (IC50 >10 μM), the Bcl-XL specific inhibitors A-1155463 and A-1331852 more potently disrupted CBcl-XL:VBad complexes with R values of ~45% and 20% respectively, corresponding to an IC50 <1.25 μM for these compounds (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The impact of A-1155463 and A-1331852 on CBcl-XL:VBimEL complexes was limited.
source: Nevertheless, their impact on CBcl-XL:VBimEL complexes was limited, confirming the high stability of CBcl-XL:VBimEL complexes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from dose-response curves.

claim: ABT-263 displaced tBid from Bcl-XL in a cell free liposome based system.
source: As expected, a concentration of ABT-263 ~10 fold higher than that of Bcl-XL displaced tBid from Bcl-XL (IC50 ~400 nM) yet had little effect on the interaction between Bcl-XL and BimL (stable at >3 μM) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data from cell-free assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: ABT-263 had little effect on the interaction between Bcl-XL and BimL in a cell free liposome based system.
source: As expected, a concentration of ABT-263 ~10 fold higher than that of Bcl-XL displaced tBid from Bcl-XL (IC50 ~400 nM) yet had little effect on the interaction between Bcl-XL and BimL (stable at >3 μM) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data from cell-free assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Expression of VBim killed MCF-7 cells.
source: Transient transfection by the requisite plasmids demonstrated that expression of VBim and VtBid killed MCF-7 cells as assessed morphologically for both cell and nuclear condensation and mitochondrial transmembrane potential (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression of VtBid killed MCF-7 cells.
source: Transient transfection by the requisite plasmids demonstrated that expression of VBim and VtBid killed MCF-7 cells as assessed morphologically for both cell and nuclear condensation and mitochondrial transmembrane potential (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression of VBad had little effect on cell death in MCF-7 cells.
source: In contrast, expression of VBad had little effect on cell death in this cell line suggesting that inhibition of Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL is not sufficient to induce apoptosis in MCF-7 cells.
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data.

claim: Inhibition of Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL is not sufficient to induce apoptosis in MCF-7 cells.
source: In contrast, expression of VBad had little effect on cell death in this cell line suggesting that inhibition of Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL is not sufficient to induce apoptosis in MCF-7 cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that VBad expression did not kill MCF-7 cells.

claim: Cells expressing CBcl-XL were highly resistant to apoptosis induced by TNFα and cycloheximide.
source: As expected, untransfected MCF-7 cells were efficiently killed while cells expressing either CBcl-XL or CBcl-2 were highly resistant to this well-established method for the induction of apoptosis (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Cells expressing CBcl-2 were highly resistant to apoptosis induced by TNFα and cycloheximide.
source: As expected, untransfected MCF-7 cells were efficiently killed while cells expressing either CBcl-XL or CBcl-2 were highly resistant to this well-established method for the induction of apoptosis (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MCF-7 cells were largely resistant to inhibition of Bcl-2 and/or Bcl-XL.
source: Consistent with the results demonstrating resistance to Bad, MCF-7 cells were largely resistant to inhibition of Bcl-2 and/or Bcl-XL (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data with BH3-mimetics shown in Figure 3D.

claim: MCF-7 cells were sensitive to inhibition of MCL-1.
source: In contrast, MCF-7 cells were sensitive to inhibition of MCL-1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data with MCL-1 inhibitor shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Overexpression of CBcl-XL protected MCF-7 cells from the MCL-1 inhibitor S-63845.
source: Moreover, overexpression of CBcl-XL or CBcl-2 protected MCF-7 cells from the MCL-1 inhibitor S-63845, likely by inhibiting pro-apoptotic proteins displaced by the BH3-mimetic from MCL-1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Overexpression of CBcl-2 protected MCF-7 cells from the MCL-1 inhibitor S-63845.
source: Moreover, overexpression of CBcl-XL or CBcl-2 protected MCF-7 cells from the MCL-1 inhibitor S-63845, likely by inhibiting pro-apoptotic proteins displaced by the BH3-mimetic from MCL-1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Truncation of the N-terminus of BimEL had little impact on Bim binding to Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
source: Truncation of the N-terminus of BimEL (VBimEL-dN) had little impact on Bim binding (Table 1)
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Table 1.

claim: Replacing the BH3 region in Bad with that in BimEL increased RABT-263 compared with VBad.
source: but replacing the BH3 region in Bad with that in BimEL (VBad-BimEL) increased RABT-263 compared with VBad.
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data.

claim: Deletion of the C-terminal sequence (CTS) from BimEL resulted in significant decreases in RABT-263 and RBH3-2A.
source: Unexpectedly, deletion of the C-terminal sequence (CTS) resulted in significant decreases in RABT-263 and RBH3-2A (Figure 4B–C and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 4B-C and Table 1.

claim: Both BH3 and CTS sequences contribute to Bim binding anti-apoptotic proteins.
source: Thus, both BH3 and CTS sequences contribute to Bim binding anti-apoptotic proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from deletion mutants.

claim: Deletion of the CTS from BimL reduced the apparent affinity for binding to Bcl-XL.
source: When assayed directly, in incubations containing mitochondria, deletion of the CTS from BimL reduced the apparent affinity for binding to Bcl-XL (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data from cell-free assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: BimL-dCTS was less effective at displacing tBid from Bcl-XL compared to BimL.
source: As predicted from the reduced affinity of this interaction, BimL-dCTS was also less effective at displacing tBid and activated Bax from Bcl-XL (Figure 5D and E, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by FRET displacement assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: BimL-dCTS was less effective at displacing activated Bax from Bcl-XL compared to BimL.
source: As predicted from the reduced affinity of this interaction, BimL-dCTS was also less effective at displacing tBid and activated Bax from Bcl-XL (Figure 5D and E, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by FRET displacement assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Substitution of the h0 sequence with WAA reduced RABT-263 for VBad-Bim to CBcl-XL from 98% to 79%.
source: Substitution of the h0 sequence with WAA reduced RABT-263 for VBad-Bim to CBcl-XL from 98% (95% Confidence Interval (CI) 6%) to 79% (CI 6%).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data.

claim: Substitution of I146 with Y decreased RABT-263 for VBad-Bim to 83%.
source: Similarly, substitution of I146 with Y decreased RABT-263 for VBad-Bim to 83% (CI 5%).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data.

claim: The RABT-263 for BimEL-I146Y-dCTS was 38% compared to 69% for VBimEL-dCTS binding to CBcl-XL.
source: The RABT-263 for Bcl-XL for this mutant (BimEL-I146Y-dCTS) was 38% (CI 8%) compared to 69% (CI 5%) for VBimEL-dCTS binding to CBcl-XL suggesting a role for I146 in BimEL binding to Bcl-XL (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Localization to mitochondria and binding to anti-apoptotic proteins are independent functions of the Bim CTS.
source: Thus in cells, localization to mitochondria and binding to anti-apoptotic proteins are independent functions of the Bim CTS.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on colocalization and binding data showing no correlation.

claim: The binding of BimL-dCTS to Bcl-XL was much more sensitive to ABT-263 compared to BimL in cell-free assays.
source: Consistent with our observations in live cells, the binding of BimL-dCTS to Bcl-XL was much more sensitive to ABT-263 (IC50 ≈ 200 nM) compared to BimL (IC50 >>4 µM).
evidence: This is supported by FRET displacement data from cell-free assays.

claim: Mutation of I181, L185 and L188 in the CTS region all resulted in increased sensitivity to displacement by ABT-263.
source: Nevertheless, in this cell free assay using purified BimL and Bcl-XL, mutation of I181, L185 and L188 in the CTS region all resulted in increased sensitivity to displacement by ABT-263 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by FRET displacement data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: BimL binding to Bcl-XL in the absence of membranes was more easily displaced by ABT-263.
source: As expected (Pécot et al., 2016), BimL binding to Bcl-XL in the absence of membranes was more easily displaced by ABT-263, but still required drug concentrations greater than 1 μM (compare Figure 7D with E).
evidence: This is supported by FRET displacement data shown in Figure 7D and E, and citation.

claim: Fusion of Venus to the C-terminus of BimEL did not abolish localization of BimELV at mitochondria.
source: Fusion of Venus to the C-terminus of BimEL did not abolish localization of BimELV at mitochondria (Figure 8A and C, red bars)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 8A and C.

claim: Fusion of Venus to the C-terminus of BimEL did not impair ABT-263 resistant binding to CBcl-XL.
source: and did not impair ABT-263 resistant binding to CBcl-XL (Figure 8B–C).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 8B-C.

claim: The FLIM-FRET efficiency observed was higher for BimELV than for VBimEL binding to CBcl-XL.
source: Moreover, the FLIM-FRET efficiency observed was higher for BimELV than for VBimEL binding to CBcl-XL (Figure 8B)
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: When Bim bound to Bcl-XL in solution there were no significant changes in hydrophobicity at any of the positions of the NBD probe.
source: When Bim bound to Bcl-XL in solution there were no significant changes in hydrophobicity at any of the positions of the probe suggesting that during complex formation these residues do not become sufficiently buried to be protected from water (Figure 9A, diagrammed in 9C).
evidence: This is supported by NBD fluorescence data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: When BimL bound to liposomes the NBD fluorescence increased at positions 179–182 and 191–195.
source: In contrast, when BimL bound to liposomes the NBD fluorescence increased at positions 179–182 and 191–195 suggesting that these two regions anchor the CTS to the lipid bilayer (Figure 9D, diagrammed in 9F).
evidence: This is supported by NBD fluorescence data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: Complex formation with Bcl-XL on the membrane did not markedly change the pattern of which amino acids increased in hydrophobicity.
source: Complex formation with Bcl-XL on the membrane did not markedly change the pattern of which amino acids increased in hydrophobicity, suggesting that complex formation does not change the way the Bim CTS interacts with membranes substantially (Figure 9G diagrammed in 9I).
evidence: This is supported by NBD fluorescence data shown in Figure 9G.

claim: When both Bcl-XL and liposomes were added the entire Bim CTS was protected from iodide.
source: In contrast, when both Bcl-XL and liposomes were added the entire Bim CTS was protected from iodide (Figure 9H, Figure 9—figure supplement 1) strongly suggesting that on membranes Bcl-XL binds to or at least covers-up the central region of the Bim CTS (diagrammed in Figure 9I).
evidence: This is supported by iodide quenching data shown in Figure 9H and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exchanging L185 with other amino acids with hydrophobic or polar non-charged side-chains did not affect the response of CBcl-XL:VBimEL-mutant complexes to BH3-2A mutations significantly.
source: In general, exchanging L185 with other amino acids with hydrophobic or polar non-charged side-chains (G, F, M, and S) did not affect the response of CBcl-XL:VBimEL-mutant complexes to BH3-2A mutations significantly, except for the L185A mutant that displayed increased binding affinity (increased RBH3-2A) (Figure 9J and Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 9J and Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: Replacing L185 with hydrophilic residues decreased RBH3-2A by ~30–60%.
source: However, replacing L185 with hydrophilic residues (H, R, D or E) decreased RBH3-2A, by ~30–60%, comparable to truncation of the CTS at position 185 (L185stop) or deletion of the entire CTS region (VBimEL-dCTS, Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 9J and referenced in Figure 4C.

claim: L185 interacts with Bcl-XL through hydrophobic interactions.
source: These results strongly suggest that L185 interacts with Bcl-XL through hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on mutagenesis data showing that hydrophobic residues are tolerated while charged residues are not.

claim: The increased binding affinity of Bim compared to Bad for Bcl-XL is primarily due to the combined effect of interactions with both the Bim BH3 region and the central hydrophobic region of the Bim CTS.
source: Although previous results ascribed an increased apparent affinity to binding to membranes (Pécot et al., 2016) our results demonstrate that the increased binding affinity of Bim compared to Bad for Bcl-XL is primarily due to the combined effect of interactions with both the Bim BH3 region (residues 140–160) and the central hydrophobic region of the Bim CTS (residues 184–190).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from the study and comparison with previous literature.

claim: The increase in affinity due to binding to membranes is relatively small.
source: While our data also confirm that the interaction occurs optimally at the membrane, the increase in affinity due to binding to membranes is relatively small (Figure 7D–E).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of FRET data with and without membranes shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: The two Bcl-XL binding sites in Bim confer resistance to the inhibitors ABT-263, A-1155463 and A-1331852.
source: Together the two Bcl-XL binding sites in Bim confer resistance to the inhibitors ABT-263, A-1155463 and A-1331852 (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The importance of residues within the BH3-region of Bim other than those at the h2 and h4 positions in binding to Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 was not detected in previous studies using BH3 peptides.
source: The importance of residues within the BH3-region of Bim other than those at the h2 and h4 positions in binding to Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 (Figure 6) was not detected in previous studies using BH3 peptides.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous literature and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: In live cells the h0 group WAA and h1 residue I146 contribute to the binding of Bim to both Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
source: Substitution of candidate residues within the h0-h4 region of the Bim BH3 sequence with the ones in the Bad BH3 revealed that in live cells the h0 group WAA and h1 residue I146 contribute to the binding of Bim to both Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Table 1.

claim: The residues at h0 and h1 account for part of the increased affinity of binding of anti-apoptotic proteins by Bim compared to Bad.
source: Because the residues at h2 and h4 are the same in Bad and Bim, the residues at h0 and h1 account for part of the increased affinity of binding of anti-apoptotic proteins by Bim compared to Bad.
evidence: This is an inference based on mutagenesis data.

claim: The additional interactions of the Bim BH3 region and the BIM CTS contributed roughly equally to the affinity of the interaction between Bim and Bcl-XL.
source: In sum the additional interactions of the Bim BH3 region and the BIM CTS contributed roughly equally to the affinity of the interaction between Bim and Bcl-XL (Figure 4B, compare VBimEL-Bad and VBimEL-dCTS).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Deletion of the Bim CTS and mutation of h2 and h4 in the BH3 region of Bim almost eliminated binding to both Bcl-XL and Bcl-2.
source: Together deletion of the Bim CTS and mutation of h2 and h4 in the BH3 region of Bim almost eliminated binding to both Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by FLIM-FRET data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The Bim CTS directly contributes to interactions with Bcl-XL.
source: Moreover, the Bim CTS directly contributes to interactions with Bcl-XL (Figure 5 and Figure 7D–E)
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 5 and FRET data shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: Much of the CTS interaction with Bcl-XL is due to residue L185.
source: and much of this interaction is due to residue L185 (Figure 9).
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis and NBD fluorescence data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The interaction of Bim with Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 is more reminiscent of a double-bolt lock with binding mediated by two distant interacting surfaces.
source: Thus unlike conventional lock and key models, the interaction of Bim with Bcl-XL and Bcl-2 is more reminiscent of a double-bolt lock with binding mediated by two distant interacting surfaces (separated by ~40 residues) working together.
evidence: This is a conceptual model based on experimental data.

claim: The Bim CTS does not adopt the previously proposed transmembrane topology.
source: Our re-evaluation of the Bim CTS not only challenges the conventional belief that the sequence only functions to bring and keep Bim at the outer mitochondrial membrane (O'Connor et al., 1998; Terrones et al., 2008) but suggests that the Bim CTS does not adopt the previously proposed transmembrane topology (Petros et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and comparison with previous literature.

claim: The CTS is pinned to the membrane by hydrophobic sequences at either end while the middle is exposed to the cytoplasmic environment.
source: Instead, the CTS is pinned to the membrane by hydrophobic sequences at either end while the middle is exposed to the cytoplasmic environment (Figure 9D–F).
evidence: This is supported by NBD fluorescence and iodide quenching data shown in Figure 9D-F.

claim: The central region of the Bim CTS may bind to the membrane surface electrostatically via two Arg residues.
source: We speculate that this topology allows the central region of the Bim CTS to bind to the membrane surface electrostatically via two Arg residues (Figure 7B–C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is speculation based on the presence of Arg residues and mutagenesis data.

claim: Substitution of Arg residues with Ala decreased localization of the protein to membranes.
source: This hypothesis is consistent with our demonstration that substitution of these Arg residues with Ala decreased localization of the protein to membranes (Figure 7B–C)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 7B-C.

claim: The Bim CTS functions as an entirely new type of membrane binding domain.
source: This insight suggests the Bim CTS functions as an entirely new type of membrane binding domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the novel topology and binding properties observed.
